title: Several Work Orders for One Customer: Pricing, Queue and Payment
content:
# Bench Standing Order: Several Work Orders for One Customer

Where one customer of the Belrose Workshop Repair and Resizing Service has several work orders running, each is priced, authorised and delivered on its own and no balance is moved between them.

## The queue across a customer's pieces

The bench queue is worked in the order the service levels rank, so a piece at a higher-ranked level overtakes one taken in earlier at a lower-ranked level. The rank of each level, and the turnaround each level targets, are the level's own figures.

## Payments

A payment taken at the counter is applied to the work order it is presented against and never spread across the customer's other running orders.

## Pieces finished together

Where the customer asks for several pieces to be finished together, the promised date of the set is the latest promised date among them, and each order keeps its own charges.

## How many of a customer's orders are running

The orders counted as running for a customer are those standing at intake, estimated, awaiting authorization, in workshop or ready for pickup, counted as at the handling date with no look-back.

## A hypothetical set

A customer has three pieces at the bench, promised back on the 9th, the 14th and the 20th of a month, and asks for all three together. The promised date of the set is the 20th, the latest of the three, and each of the three orders still carries its own charges: a payment presented against the piece promised on the 14th goes to that order alone.
